content.comment_body: Hello [product_name] community, Is there a method to identify all users currently connected to the web server of a [product_name] or its networking ports? For instance: - port 102 (used by an Android HMI app and similar services), - ports 80 or 8080 (for the [product_name] web server), - and the [product_name] app port, which I'm not certain about. I am aware that access can be restricted to a specific number of IP addresses (up to 8, I believe) using the [product_name] configuration application. Lastly, is it possible to create a different user account for the web server aside from the default user, in order to delay unauthorized access and possibly improve resistance to brute-force attacks? Ideally, I’d like to give some users limited authorization rather than full access, similar to user management with different permission levels. Thank you for your assistance. [user_name]

Hello everyone, The only approach I found effective is to install a firewall to monitor the relevant ports, which allows you to estimate who is trying to access and when. This can help identify potential DoS or brute-force attempts on your PLC, since most PLCs like [product_name] lack automated defenses against such attacks. This security gap is a significant concern for these devices. Thanks in advance. [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are concerned about limited user management and security options for the web server of [product_name] devices. They note the inability to see connected users, create multiple user accounts, and prevent brute-force or DoS attacks. Restrictions on allowed IP addresses and the absence of granular access controls are seen as significant security limitations affecting these devices.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to have the ability to view all users connected to the [product_name] web server, easily handle user accounts, including creating additional users, and to benefit from stronger safeguards against brute-force and DoS attacks.
